entries.label: Example 2
entries.title: Split one column proportionally
entries.paper: ISIT 2026, p. 3, Section III-A, Example 2 and Equations (11)–(12).
entries.statement_html: For 0 < β < 1, applying PPS with ratio 1/2 to the second column of the common three-input, five-output channel in Equation (11) gives the six-output channel in Equation (12).
entries.proof_html: The fixture applies the actual PPS constructor to the source channel, supplies the strict split-ratio witnesses, and proves equality of the entire resulting real matrix with the displayed target. Additional checks cover every probability entry, active outputs, singularity and row sums.
entries.qualifier_html: This is a private checked fixture, not a separately exported example theorem. The strict parameter range keeps every source output active; the endpoint parameters 0 and 1 are not instances of this active-channel fixture. Paper column labels are translated to zero-based Lean indices.

evidence.label: Private PPS fixture with legality witnesses

evidence.needle: Activity is checked for every output
evidence.label: Activity, singularity and row-sum checks

depends.why: The example instantiates the legal proportional-split operation on an active singular channel.

entries.label: Example 3
entries.title: Merge columns with the same support
entries.paper: ISIT 2026, p. 3, Section III-A, Example 3 and Equations (11), (13).
entries.statement_html: For 0 < β < 1, applying PPM to the fourth and fifth columns of Equation (11) gives the four-output channel in Equation (13). The merged columns have the same support.
entries.proof_html: The fixture supplies the ordering and common-support witnesses to the actual PPM constructor. It checks all entries through a whole-matrix equality and also verifies the resulting channel's active outputs, singularity and row sums.
entries.qualifier_html: This is a private fixture, not public example API. The strict parameter range is required by the active-output presentation. The merge includes the final source column, using the full source-index range clarified in the extended v16 companion; paper indices are converted to zero-based Lean indices.

evidence.label: Private PPM fixture, including the final column

evidence.needle: The printed operations' exact legality witnesses
evidence.label: Explicit operation-legality checks

depends.why: The example instantiates proportional merging with its common-support and distinct-column requirements.

entries.label: Example 4
entries.title: Split a column's support
entries.paper: ISIT 2026, p. 3, Section III-A, Example 4 and Equations (11), (14).
entries.statement_html: For 0 < β < 1, applying VPS to the first column of Equation (11), with input mask (1, 1, 0), gives the six-output channel in Equation (14). Both parts of the split contain a nonzero entry.
entries.proof_html: The private source fixture provides a supported input on each side of the mask. The VPS constructor therefore produces two active columns; a complete real-matrix equality checks the intended ordering and every target entry. Further fixtures verify activity, singularity and row sums.
entries.qualifier_html: The example is checked by private fixtures rather than exposed as stable public API. Its source parameter satisfies 0 < β < 1. The Boolean mask is interpreted on zero-based Lean input labels, with paper column 1 represented by index 0.

evidence.label: Private VPS fixture with both nonempty pieces

evidence.needle: The printed operations' exact legality witnesses
evidence.label: Mask-support and legality checks

depends.why: The example instantiates support splitting with a supported input on each side of the mask.

entries.label: Example 5
entries.title: Merge equal-valued disjoint columns
entries.paper: ISIT 2026, p. 3, Section III-A, Example 5 and Equations (11), (15).
entries.statement_html: For 0 < β < 1, applying VPM to the first and third columns of Equation (11) gives the four-output channel in Equation (15). Those columns have disjoint supports and equal nonzero value 1 − β.
entries.proof_html: The fixture proves the equality of the two column values and their support disjointness before invoking VPM. A whole-matrix equality verifies the result, supplemented by exact probability-entry, activity, singularity and normalization checks.
entries.qualifier_html: This is a private checked example, not a public theorem alias. Its legality depends on 0 < β < 1 and on both VPM guards; it is not a claim that arbitrary disjoint columns may be merged. Paper labels 1 and 3 become Lean indices 0 and 2.

evidence.label: Private VPM fixture with equal-value and disjointness witnesses

evidence.needle: The printed operations' exact legality witnesses
evidence.label: Column-value and disjoint-support checks

depends.why: The example instantiates value-preserving merging under its equal-value and disjoint-support conditions.

entries.label: Example 6
entries.title: The five partitions of three inputs
entries.paper: ISIT 2026, p. 4 right, Section IV-A, Example 6 (three-input partitions).
entries.statement_html: A three-element input set has exactly five partitions: the single whole block, three choices of a pair together with the remaining singleton, and the partition into three singletons.
entries.proof_html: The fixture proves an exhaustive case split for every exact partition, then shows that the paper-ordered list is injective and surjective. The resulting equivalence with Fin 5 proves the cardinality-five check used by the incidence examples.
entries.qualifier_html: This is an exact three-input fixture with private enumeration helpers, not a general Bell-number formula or a public example API. The general Bell-count statement cited in the paper remains intentionally outside the formalized scope.

evidence.label: Paper-ordered partition enumeration and bijection proofs

depends.why: The example enumerates the exact partitions used as full incidence-system column indices.

entries.label: Example 7
entries.title: The three-input incidence matrix
entries.paper: ISIT 2026, p. 4 right, Section IV-A, Example 7 and Equation (17).
entries.statement_html: Indexing the seven nonempty input patterns and the five exact partitions in the paper's orders produces the displayed 7 × 5 incidence matrix. Every one of its 35 entries is checked. An additional fixture verifies how a proper reduced 4 × 2 system is obtained by selecting its occurring-pattern rows and admissible-partition columns.
entries.proof_html: Private row and column equivalences connect the finite paper coordinates to semantic patterns and partitions. Exhaustive entry calculations establish the full matrix equality. A separate reindexing equality identifies the reduced fixture with the specified submatrix of that full matrix.
entries.qualifier_html: These are private coordinate fixtures, not newly exported example declarations. The full and reduced incidence systems retain distinct index types; the extra reduced-submatrix check does not identify them or supply a general LP solver.

evidence.label: Exact paper row and column equivalences
Proper reduced 4 × 2 submatrix and exact-entry fixture

depends.why: The matrix entries express membership of nonempty patterns in exact partitions.
The full-coordinate verification uses the exhaustive five-partition enumeration and its column equivalence.

entries.label: Remark 2
entries.title: Connections to other information measures
entries.paper: ISIT 2026, p. 4 left, Remark 2 between the Theorem 1 proof and Section IV: three unnumbered displays and the final channel-synthesis sentence.
entries.statement_html: The remark discusses cited connections between perfect representability, graph entropy, the privacy-funnel quantity, the related g0 expression, and zero redundancy in channel synthesis.
entries.proof_html: No Lean proof of these external equivalences or synthesis interpretations is claimed. The coverage audit records the graph-entropy, privacy-funnel, g0 and channel-synthesis occurrences separately, rather than treating the formalized constructive theorem as a proof of them.
entries.qualifier_html: Intentionally not formalized: the cited information measures and external channel-synthesis model are outside this case study's scope. These are documentation dispositions, not missing proof placeholders. Coverage of Theorem 1 does not extend automatically to Remark 2.

evidence.label: Graph-entropy, privacy-funnel, g0 and synthesis dispositions

depends.why: The external discussion concerns channel perfect representability; this is a contextual link, not a formalized proof dependency.
